name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: Cooldown Landmines: Cross-Tenant Interference Attacks on LLM Gateways
items.dek: LiteLLM gateways sharing cooldown records allow cross-tenant attacks forcing fallback or denial; tenant-scoped cooldown with origin checks mitigates the gap.
items.unproven: attacks demonstrated on LiteLLM; effectiveness against other LLM gateway implementations and with hardened authentication policies not tested

items.title: Correct Verdicts, Flawed Reasoning: Structured Auditing of LLM-based Vulnerability Reasoning
items.dek: 60% of correct LLM vulnerability verdicts rest on fabricated reasoning; structured output auditing catches failures that free-form CoT conceals.
items.unproven: VERA's performance on proprietary or novel vulnerability classes; integration into live SAST/DAST pipelines; cost of structured output overhead at scale.

items.title: Backdooring Sparse Autoencoders
items.dek: Maliciously modified sparse autoencoders can inject code backdoors into language models without changing the model itself.
items.unproven: Supply-chain detection mechanisms and defense deployment feasibility in real SDLC pipelines not addressed.

items.title: Runaway Reaction: When Benign Skills Compose into Malicious Behavior
items.dek: Composing benign agent skills can create malicious behaviors not present in any individual skill, even after vetting.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to skill repositories tested; generalization to closed or proprietary skill ecosystems not demonstrated.

items.title: Blocking at the Boundary: Auditing Long-Horizon Agents against Staged Prompt Injection
items.dek: Claude Code and Codex are vulnerable to staged prompt injection across long workflows; blocking requires boundary action auditing before each consequential action, not pre- or post-execution screening.
items.unproven: evaluated on two model families in native runtimes; effectiveness against fine-tuned or system-prompted variants not established

items.title: VulValidate: Auditing Function-Level Vulnerability Labels with Executable Evidence
items.dek: Auditing 35,849 labeled vulnerable functions in BigVul, PrimeVul, and DiverseVul confirms 57.2%, corrects 19.0%, and reclassifies 22.3%; expert review supports 90–99% of decisions.
items.unproven: corrected dataset contains 15,890 distinct functions; representativeness of expert panel and generalization to future vulnerability datasets not established

items.title: Secure Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models
items.dek: Speculative decoding in LLMs degrades security faster than utility improves; SecureSD method proposed to recover safety.
items.unproven: theory-guided approach not yet independently validated; security implications measured on jailbreak and prompt-injection but not other threat models

items.title: Case-Level Verification in Scanner-LLM Cascades: Overcoming the Alert Aggregation Bottleneck to Expand the FRR-TPR Trade-off Space
items.dek: Case-level verification in DAST-LLM cascades breaks the false-positive-true-positive trade-off by deciding per finding instead of per alert group.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to unspecified scanner and LLM pairing; generalization to production DAST tools and enterprise alert volumes unknown.

items.title: Surviving the Router: Optimizing Skill Injections for Retrieval and Execution
items.dek: Multi-skill agents reduce injected prompt attack success by 87-97% through router competition; CORSA method recovers attacks by optimizing for retrieval and execution.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to SkillRouter benchmark and eight payload categories; unclear how findings transfer to production agent deployments with real skill libraries.

items.title: Where does a rust speedup come from? Language and algorithm effects in sliding window threat scorer
items.dek: Rust rewrite of Python threat scorer attributes 4–29× speedup to language and 11,000×+ to algorithmic change; power-law exponents reveal algorithm dominance.
items.unproven: single threat scorer implementation (SentinelSphere sliding-window calculator); generalization to other security analytics pipelines not established.

items.title: Plug-and-Play Quantum-Resistant BLE Pairing for Medical Implants via NFC Out-of-Band
items.dek: NFC-based out-of-band BLE pairing protocol performs post-quantum KEM without modifying BLE stack; IMD-class proof-of-concept demonstrates practical quantum-resistant medical implant pairing.
items.unproven: proof-of-concept testbed only; no interoperability testing with production medical devices or regulatory pathway (FDA) validation; long-term NFC eavesdropping resistance under field conditions unproven.

items.title: Lifecycle-Based Design and Evaluation of Real-Time Backup Triggers for Ransomware Damage Mitigation
items.dek: Testing file-lifecycle backup triggers against five ransomware samples shows write-time triggers reduce recoverable damage versus open-time backup.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to XFS and five specific ransomware samples; behavior on other filesystems and newer variants unknown

items.title: The Model Plants the Trigger: Answer-Side Backdoor Attacks in Multi-Turn Large Language Models
items.dek: LLMs can be backdoored via self-generated trigger words planted in dialogue history, bypassing input-sanitizing defenses at near-100% success rates.
items.unproven: demonstrated on four models in controlled dialogue setting; generalization to deployed LLM agents with real guardrails and multi-agent coordination unknown

items.title: Adaptive Model Inversion Attacks Generalize a Privacy-Robustness Tradeoff
items.dek: Model inversion attacks leak training data 1.16 to 6.59 times more on adaptive attack than standard evaluation, exposing privacy-robustness tradeoff.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to face-recognition task on FaceScrub; whether tradeoff generalizes to other domains and model architectures not shown

items.title: Does AI Help Cyber Attackers or Defenders? Evidence from Nonpublic Vulnerabilities and Subsequent Attacks
items.dek: AI models tested on nonpublic vulnerabilities show variable exploit-versus-repair performance, with 92 of 524 follow-up attacks succeeding after initial patch.
items.unproven: Whether results generalize across vulnerability classes and whether lab exploit generation tracks real attacker capability in active campaigns.

items.title: RAISED: Self-Distillation for Robustness to Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
items.dek: RAISED self-distillation mitigates prompt injection in tool-using agents by matching clean behavior without distribution drift on benign tasks.
items.unproven: Robustness against adaptive attacks or to agents in active production SDLCs; evaluation on agent types beyond the tested scenarios.

items.title: Where Did the Repair First Go Wrong? Localizing the Origins of Silent Failures in Agentic Vulnerability Repair
items.dek: Trace-based method locates where LLM repair agents first diverge from security intent in silent failures; most trace to unaddressed requirements, not code writes.
items.unproven: ground truth for 5 of 95 failures and potential labeler bias; generalization beyond SecurityEval and CVEfixes; applicability when agent frameworks lack execution traces.

items.title: Visual Grounding Safety in Vision-Language Models
items.dek: Vision-language models refuse harmful requests 31–59 percentage points more often in text form than when asked to output bounding boxes or points.
items.unproven: whether this gap persists across production deployment patterns and whether fine-tuning generalizes beyond the three benchmarks tested.

items.title: The Poisoned Conversation: Privacy-Leaking Watermarks in Unified Multimodal Models
items.dek: Malicious multimodal models can embed hidden watermarks in later-generated images keyed to earlier sensitive text in the same conversation, leaking privacy from local deployments.
items.unproven: whether detection remains feasible under adversarial watermark design and whether practical deployment scenarios encounter this threat model.

items.title: Who Is Your Agent Serving? Provider-Side Indirect Prompt Injection in Proactive Agents
items.dek: External providers can redirect proactive agents toward their targets by controlling only their own content, gaining up to 77.4 percentage-point increases in target authorization.
items.unproven: tested only on simulated user models in three controlled environments; unclear how real users would respond to such attacks in production deployment

items.title: Semantic Behavioral Watermarking: Paraphrase-Robust and Forgery-Resistant Provenance for LLM Agents
items.dek: Semantic behavioral watermarking for LLM agents resists paraphrasing and forgery better than prior schemes.
items.unproven: tested on five models and three encoders; no evidence watermark survives deliberate agent redesign or tool replacement in production

items.title: RAG-PIBench: A Leakage-Aware Benchmark for Prompt-Injection Detection in Trustworthy RAG Systems
items.dek: RAG-PIBench dataset with 4,876 examples shows DistilBERT achieves 0.896 F1 on prompt-injection detection in retrieval systems.
items.unproven: benchmark is static; does not measure generalization to injection patterns not in training distribution or to new attack techniques

items.title: Newer and Bigger, but Safer? A Longitudinal Study of the Functionality-Security Gap in LLM-Generated Code
items.authors: Thiago Santos de Moura et al.
items.dek: Longitudinal study of 32 LLMs across five open-weight families shows newer models reduce security gaps in generated code, but no family closes the gap entirely.
items.unproven: CWEval coverage (119 tasks, 31 CWEs) may not reflect OWASP Top 25 or domain-specific vulnerabilities in financial code; generative security risk depends on downstream scanning integration.

items.title: When Tools Lie: Reliability of Mathematical Agents Under Corrupted Tool Feedback
items.dek: LLM agents lose 28% accuracy when tool outputs are silently corrupted; mandatory reflection recovers full performance, optional verification does not.
items.unproven: study uses synthetic corruption framework and 31 problems; applicability to real silent tool failures and agent codebases in production SDLC undefined.

items.title: Preparing an AI-Augmented SIEM for the EU Cyber Resilience Act: A Practitioner Case Study
items.dek: Six-step CRA preparedness recipe (Scope, Asset, Evidence, Map, Gap, Audit) with traceability threads applied to AI-augmented SEUXDR SIEM on CYBERFORT platform.
items.unproven: single product case study; recipe applicability to non-AI security products and to firms without existing CYBERFORT deployment unclear; no third-party audit validation.

noise.title: Xray-core concealed a certificate verification bypass vulnerability
noise.dek: Xray-core had a certificate verification bypass; no exploitation details or patch status provided.
noise.unproven: whether the vulnerability is exploitable in reader's deployment, patch availability, or prevalence in financial services networks

noise.title: ArtCraft Apps – open-source Adobe compatible suite written in Rust
noise.dek: Open-source Adobe-compatible suite in Rust launches; no security angle identified.

noise.title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with AI [video]
noise.dek: Video on using AI for creative work scaling.
noise.unproven: outside reader's remit; not SDLC, agent security, or post-quantum work
